note: Minimal, focused secondary research. Figures are as reported by each source; market reports differ widely in methodology and values, so market sizes in the app are assumption-based and labelled as such.

sources.name: Assessment of RO Wastewater Management and Reuse, Gurugram (IJAES, 2024)
findings: 143 respondents (Gurugram); 39.8% of respondents with an RO system reuse reject water, mostly for gardening (verified; paper does not state the exact denominator)
35% said an additional storage tank could be installed (verified; the paper marks this item as non-exhaustive); 60% suggested buckets; 29% a central plumbing collection system
Paper cites 3–4 L of reject water per litre purified (~75% wastage) for conventional RO
Only 45% knew about reuse practices; ~14% would consider reuse if better technology were available; authors call for easier-to-use reuse technology

sources.name: BIS — IS 16240:2023 RO point-of-use water treatment systems
findings: Minimum recovery requirement raised from 20% to 40% to minimise water wastage

sources.name: Down To Earth — NGT order on RO systems (2019)
findings: NGT asked for RO recovery of at least 60% and restriction of RO where TDS < 500 mg/l

sources.name: Bhagwat & Munavalli (2020), Study on Feed and Reject Water Quality in RO Systems, Springer
findings: Household RO reject-water TDS ranged 279–1,616 mg/L (feed 238–1,317 mg/L)
Reject water can be reused for gardens, washing and flushing

sources.name: Havells — tips to reuse RO waste water
findings: Dilute reject water for mopping to avoid salt deposits
Utensil washing should be done only with fresh water
